sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Decaf RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Light Inside Out
sequence.text:
2
Light Inside Out
Instructions

Translate and quip the first and last sentences of the passage*.

Translate and quip all the question stems and answer choices.

Highlight the topics in the answer choices that recur across multiple questions.

Highlight the parts of the passage referenced in the question stems.

This means you should highlight the words and phrases that the Specific Reference questions call out, so they jump out to you while you're translating the passage.

Read and translate the passage.

Return to the questions and answer them.

sequence.name: Tone Training
sequence.text:
3
Tone Training
Instructions

Highlight the adjectives and adverbs in a few passages* to train yourself to notice them.

At the end of each passage, ask yourself, "How did this passage feel?" and use the adjectives and adverbs to help you.

Write down your answer to how this passage feels before doing the questions.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Will This Help Me?

THIS WILL HELP YOU IF

You're easing your way into answering questions after your RC translation and beginning to explore the RC section overall.

SKIP FOR NOW IF

You feel comfortable and confident retaining the details of the passage Translation throughout the answer choices.

CHALLENGE INDEX

LEVEL
Beginner
FREQUENCY
Daily Foundation
STUDY BLOCK LENGTH
2-4 hours
Schedule (3 workouts)

Ensure you complete the workouts in order to benefit the most from this routine.

1
Decaf RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
2
Light Inside Out
3
Tone Training
Instructions

Highlight the adjectives and adverbs in a few passages* to train yourself to notice them.

At the end of each passage, ask yourself, "How did this passage feel?" and use the adjectives and adverbs to help you.

Write down your answer to how this passage feels before doing the questions.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're a little less scared of RC now, so we can move our Decaf to a warmup and let you choose what Translation style you want to use on your Light Inside Out. 

If you want to stick with Decaf, that's fine, but feel free to move to Cappuccino or Caffeinated if that's more comfortable for you. 

Light Inside Out is a little less work than Modified Inside Out, so you should still feel comfortable with RC without as much energy expenditure. It still spoils the passage, so there's no worries there. 

We add some Tone Training to get you used to feeling the author's emotions through the passage. That way you won't be as intimidated when you have to do Tone questions in a timed environment.

How This Should Be Done

This is another Routine where I really don't want you to rush.

This Routine might take a little less time than the Make RC Easy Routine, but slow and steady wins the race, especially if you're changing the RC Translation Drill away from Decaf.

Remember the point of the I'm Afraid of RC Routine Progression is to fix your RC mindset. If the Routine isn't helping your mindset, it's not doing its job.

How to Move On

If you feel less fear (but still a little bit of fear) toward RC, move on to the Learn to Love RC Routine, the next Routine in the I'm Afraid of RC Routine Progression.

If you don't feel any fear toward RC, move on to any of the I Just Want to Focus on RC Routine Progressions.
